name: Mailchimp
description: Mailchimp is an email marketing and automation platform providing campaign templates, audience segmentation, and performance analytics to drive engagement and conversions

tools.name: Add automation
tools.description: Create a new classic abandoned cart automation in your Mailchimp account. This action creates an automation workflow that sends emails to customers who have abandoned their shopping cart. Requires a connected e-commerce store and an audience/list. Prerequisites: - A Mailchimp audience/list (use MAILCHIMP_ADD_LIST or MAILCHIMP_GET_LISTS_INFO) - A connected e-commerce store (use MAILCHIMP_ADD_STORE or MAILCHIMP_LIST_STORES) Note: Classic automations are only available to paid Mailchimp accounts that have previously created a classic automation. Currently only the 'abandonedCart' workflow type is supported via the API.

inputs.name: settings__reply__to
inputs.about: The email address that recipients can reply to (e.g., 'support@yourcompany.com').

inputs.name: recipients__list__id
inputs.about: The unique ID of the Mailchimp audience/list that this automation will target. Required for creating an automation. Get this from MAILCHIMP_GET_LISTS_INFO.

inputs.name: settings__from__name
inputs.about: The sender name that appears in the "From" field of automation emails (e.g., 'Your Company Name'). Not an email address.

inputs.name: recipients__store__id
inputs.about: The unique ID of the connected e-commerce store. Required for abandonedCart workflow type to enable cart tracking. Get this from MAILCHIMP_LIST_STORES.

inputs.name: trigger__settings__workflow__type
inputs.about: The type of classic automation workflow to create. Currently only 'abandonedCart' is supported via the API. This triggers emails when a customer abandons their shopping cart.

tools.name: Add batch webhook
tools.description: Configure a webhook that will fire whenever any batch request completes processing. You may only have a maximum of 20 batch webhooks.

inputs.name: url
inputs.about: A valid URL for the batch webhook. Mailchimp will POST data to this URL when a batch operation completes processing. Must be a publicly accessible HTTPS URL.

inputs.name: enabled
inputs.about: Whether the webhook should be enabled to receive requests. Defaults to True if not specified.

tools.name: Add campaign
tools.description: Create a new Mailchimp campaign.

inputs.name: type
inputs.about: There are four types of [campaigns](https://mailchimp.com/help/getting-started-with-campaigns/) you can create in Mailchimp. A/B Split campaigns have been deprecated and variate campaigns should be used instead.

inputs.name: content_type
inputs.about: How the campaign"s content is put together. The old drag and drop editor uses "template" while the new editor uses "multichannel". Defaults to template.

inputs.name: settings__title
inputs.about: The title of the campaign.

inputs.name: tracking__opens
inputs.about: Whether to [track opens](https://mailchimp.com/help/about-open-tracking/). Defaults to `true`. Cannot be set to false for variate campaigns.

inputs.name: settings__to__name
inputs.about: The campaign"s custom "To" name. Typically the first name [audience field](https://mailchimp.com/help/getting-started-with-merge-tags/).

inputs.name: tracking__ecomm360
inputs.about: Whether to enable e-commerce tracking.

inputs.name: settings__reply__to
inputs.about: The reply-to email address for the campaign. Note: while this field is not required for campaign creation, it is required for sending.

inputs.name: social__card__title
inputs.about: The title for the card. Typically the subject line of the campaign.

inputs.name: tracking__clicktale
inputs.about: The custom slug for [ClickTale](https://mailchimp.com/help/additional-tracking-options-for-campaigns/) tracking (max of 50 bytes).

inputs.name: recipients__list__id
inputs.about: The unique list id.

inputs.name: rss__opts__feed__url
inputs.about: The URL for the RSS feed.

inputs.name: rss__opts__frequency
inputs.about: The frequency of the RSS Campaign.

inputs.name: settings__folder__id
inputs.about: If the campaign is listed in a folder, the id for that folder.

inputs.name: settings__from__name
inputs.about: The "from" name on the campaign (not an email address).

inputs.name: settings__auto__tweet
inputs.about: Automatically tweet a link to the [campaign archive](https://mailchimp.com/help/about-email-campaign-archives-and-pages/) page when the campaign is sent.

inputs.name: settings__inline__css
inputs.about: Automatically inline the CSS included with the campaign content.

inputs.name: settings__authenticate
inputs.about: Whether Mailchimp [authenticated](https://mailchimp.com/help/about-email-authentication/) the campaign. Defaults to `true`.

inputs.name: settings__auto__footer
inputs.about: Automatically append Mailchimp"s [default footer](https://mailchimp.com/help/about-campaign-footers/) to the campaign.

inputs.name: settings__fb__comments
inputs.about: Allows Facebook comments on the campaign (also force-enables the Campaign Archive toolbar). Defaults to `true`.

inputs.name: settings__template__id
inputs.about: The id of the template to use.

inputs.name: tracking__html__clicks
inputs.about: Whether to [track clicks](https://mailchimp.com/help/enable-and-view-click-tracking/) in the HTML version of the campaign. Defaults to `true`. Cannot be set to false for variate campaigns.

inputs.name: tracking__text__clicks
inputs.about: Whether to [track clicks](https://mailchimp.com/help/enable-and-view-click-tracking/) in the plain-text version of the campaign. Defaults to `true`. Cannot be set to false for variate campaigns.

inputs.name: settings__preview__text
inputs.about: The preview text for the campaign.

inputs.name: settings__subject__line
inputs.about: The subject line for the campaign.

inputs.name: settings__auto__fb__post
inputs.about: An array of [Facebook](https://mailchimp.com/help/connect-or-disconnect-the-facebook-integration/) page ids to auto-post to.

inputs.name: social__card__image__url
inputs.about: The url for the header image for the card.

inputs.name: tracking__capsule__notes
inputs.about: Update contact notes for a campaign based on subscriber email addresses.

inputs.name: tracking__goal__tracking
inputs.about: Deprecated

inputs.name: rss__opts__schedule__hour
inputs.about: The hour to send the campaign in local time. Acceptable hours are 0-23. For example, "4" would be 4am in [your account"s default time zone](https://mailchimp.com/help/set-account-defaults/).

inputs.name: social__card__description
inputs.about: A short summary of the campaign to display.

inputs.name: settings__use__conversation
inputs.about: Use Mailchimp Conversation feature to manage out-of-office replies.

inputs.name: tracking__google__analytics
inputs.about: The custom slug for [Google Analytics](https://mailchimp.com/help/integrate-google-analytics-with-mailchimp/) tracking (max of 50 bytes).

inputs.name: tracking__salesforce__notes
inputs.about: Update contact notes for a campaign based on subscriber email addresses.

inputs.name: variate__settings__test__size
inputs.about: The percentage of recipients to send the test combinations to, must be a value between 10 and 100.

inputs.name: variate__settings__wait__time
inputs.about: The number of minutes to wait before choosing the winning campaign. The value of wait_time must be greater than 0 and in whole hours, specified in minutes.

inputs.name: rss__opts__constrain__rss__img
inputs.about: Whether to add CSS to images in the RSS feed to constrain their width in campaigns.

inputs.name: tracking__salesforce__campaign
inputs.about: Create a campaign in a connected Salesforce account.

inputs.name: variate__settings__from__names
inputs.about: The possible from names. The number of from_names provided must match the number of reply_to_addresses. If no from_names are provided, settings.from_name will be used.

inputs.name: variate__settings__send__times
inputs.about: The possible send times to test. The times provided should be in the format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS. If send_times are provided to test, the test_size will be set to 100% and winner_criteria will be ignored.

inputs.name: recipients__segment__opts__match
inputs.about: Segment match type.

inputs.name: variate__settings__subject__lines
inputs.about: The possible subject lines to test. If no subject lines are provided, settings.subject_line will be used.

inputs.name: variate__settings__winner__criteria
inputs.about: The combination that performs the best. This may be determined automatically by click rate, open rate, or total revenue -- or you may choose manually based on the reporting data you find the most valuable. For Multivariate Campaigns testing send_time, winner_criteria is ignored. For Multivariate Cam

inputs.name: recipients__segment__opts__conditions
inputs.about: Segment match conditions. There are multiple possible types, see the [condition types documentation](https://mailchimp.com/developer/marketing/docs/alternative-schemas/#segment-condition-schemas).

inputs.name: rss__opts__schedule__weekly__send__day
inputs.about: The day of the week to send a weekly RSS Campaign.

inputs.name: variate__settings__reply__to__addresses
inputs.about: The possible reply-to addresses. The number of reply_to_addresses provided must match the number of from_names. If no reply_to_addresses are provided, settings.reply_to will be used.

inputs.name: rss__opts__schedule__daily__send__friday
inputs.about: Sends the daily RSS Campaign on Fridays.

inputs.name: rss__opts__schedule__daily__send__monday
inputs.about: Sends the daily RSS Campaign on Mondays.

inputs.name: rss__opts__schedule__daily__send__sunday
inputs.about: Sends the daily RSS Campaign on Sundays.

inputs.name: rss__opts__schedule__monthly__send__date
inputs.about: The day of the month to send a monthly RSS Campaign. Acceptable days are 0-31, where "0" is always the last day of a month. Months with fewer than the selected number of days will not have an RSS campaign sent out that day. For example, RSS Campaigns set to send on the 30th will not go out in Februa

inputs.name: rss__opts__schedule__daily__send__tuesday
inputs.about: Sends the daily RSS Campaign on Tuesdays.

inputs.name: rss__opts__schedule__daily__send__saturday
inputs.about: Sends the daily RSS Campaign on Saturdays.

inputs.name: rss__opts__schedule__daily__send__thursday
inputs.about: Sends the daily RSS Campaign on Thursdays.

inputs.name: rss__opts__schedule__daily__send__wednesday
inputs.about: Sends the daily RSS Campaign on Wednesdays.

inputs.name: recipients__segment__opts__saved__segment__id
inputs.about: The id for an existing saved segment.

tools.name: Add Campaign Feedback
tools.description: Add feedback on a specific Mailchimp campaign. Use this to post comments, notes, or feedback while collaborating on a campaign with your team. The feedback can be associated with a specific content block or applied to the campaign as a whole.

inputs.name: message
inputs.about: The content of the feedback message. This is the text of the feedback comment.

inputs.name: block_id
inputs.about: The block ID for the editable block that the feedback addresses. Optional - omit if providing general feedback on the campaign.

inputs.name: campaign_id
inputs.about: The unique ID for the campaign. You can get this from the List Campaigns endpoint or when creating a campaign.

inputs.name: is_complete
inputs.about: Whether the feedback item is complete. Set to true to mark as resolved, false otherwise. Defaults to false if not provided.

tools.name: Add campaign folder
tools.description: Create a new campaign folder to organize email campaigns in Mailchimp. Campaign folders help organize your email marketing campaigns into logical groups. Returns the created folder's ID, name, and initial campaign count (0).

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The name for the new campaign folder. This is used to organize campaigns in the Mailchimp interface.

tools.name: Add cart
tools.description: Add a new cart to a store.

inputs.name: id
inputs.about: A unique identifier for the cart.

inputs.name: lines
inputs.about: An array of the cart's line items. Each line item must include: 'id' (unique identifier for the line item), 'product_id' (ID of the product in your store), 'product_variant_id' (ID of the product variant), 'quantity' (number of items), and 'price' (price of the item as a number). Example: [{'id': 'l

inputs.name: campaign_id

inputs.name: order_total

inputs.name: currency_code

inputs.about: The customer's first name.

inputs.name: customer__address__city

inputs.name: customer__opt__in__status
inputs.about: Required. The customer's opt-in status. inputs.about: The customer's country.

inputs.name: customer__address__address1
inputs.about: The mailing address of the customer.

inputs.name: customer__address__address2
inputs.about: An additional field for the customer's mailing address.

inputs.name: customer__address__province
inputs.about: The customer's state name or normalized province.

inputs.name: customer__address__postal__code
inputs.about: The customer's postal or zip code.

inputs.name: customer__address__country__code
inputs.about: The two-letter ISO country code for the customer's country (e.g., 'US', 'DE').

inputs.name: customer__address__province__code
inputs.about: The two-letter code for the customer's province or state.

tools.name: Add cart line item
tools.description: Add a new line item to an existing cart.

inputs.name: id
inputs.about: A unique identifier for the cart line item. Must be unique within the cart.

inputs.name: price
inputs.about: The price per unit for the cart line item in the store's currency.

inputs.name: cart_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the cart to add the line item to.

inputs.name: quantity
inputs.about: The quantity of this product variant to add to the cart. Must be a positive integer.

inputs.name: store_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the e-commerce store.

inputs.name: product_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the product. The product must already exist in the store.

inputs.name: product_variant_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the product variant. The variant must exist for the specified product.

tools.name: Add connected site
tools.description: Create a new Mailchimp connected site. Connected sites allow you to track website visitor activity and integrate with Mailchimp's marketing features. After adding a connected site, you'll receive a tracking script (site_script) that should be installed on your website to enable visitor tracking.

inputs.name: domain
inputs.about: The full domain name of the connected site (e.g., 'example.com' or 'shop.mystore.com'). This is the website URL where the Mailchimp tracking script will be installed.

inputs.name: foreign_id
inputs.about: A unique identifier for the connected site that you define. This ID is used to reference the site in subsequent API calls. Example: 'my-website-001' or 'store-12345'.

tools.name: Add contact to audience
tools.description: Tool to create a new omni-channel contact in a Mailchimp audience. Use when adding contacts with email and/or SMS channels to an audience.

inputs.name: tags
inputs.about: An array of tag names to add to the contact. This operation is append-only; existing tags will be preserved, and only new tags from this array will be added.

inputs.name: language
inputs.about: The subscriber's language preference as a two-letter ISO 639-1 code (e.g., 'en', 'es', 'fr').

inputs.name: data_mode
inputs.about: Data processing mode.

inputs.name: audience_id
inputs.about: The unique ID for the audience. Get this from the Mailchimp account or via the list audiences endpoint.

inputs.name: sms_channel
inputs.about: SMS channel details for a contact.

inputs.name: merge_fields
inputs.about: A dictionary of merge fields where the keys are the merge tags (like FNAME, LNAME). Values are strings representing the field values. See the Merge Fields documentation for more about the structure.

inputs.name: email_channel
inputs.about: Email channel details for a contact.

inputs.name: merge_field_validation_mode
inputs.about: Merge field validation mode.

tools.name: Add domain to account
tools.description: Add a sending domain to the Mailchimp account for email verification. This action adds a new domain to your Mailchimp account and initiates the verification process by sending a verification code to the specified email address. After calling this action, use the 'verify_domain' action with the received verification code to complete the domain verification process.

inputs.name: verification_email
inputs.about: The email address at the domain you want to verify (e.g., 'admin@yourdomain.com'). A verification code will be sent to this email address to confirm domain ownership. You must have access to this email inbox to complete the verification process.

tools.name: Add event
tools.description: Add an event for a list member. Use this action to track contact activity and behavior outside of email campaigns. Events can be used for segmentation and triggering automation workflows. Common use cases: - Track purchases, signups, or page visits - Record custom milestones or achievements - Import historical events with is_syncing=true to avoid triggering automations Note: Returns 204 No Content on success (empty response body).

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The name for this type of event (e.g., 'purchased', 'visited', 'signup_completed'). Must be 2-30 characters in length. Use lowercase letters, numbers, and underscores only.

inputs.name: list_id
inputs.about: The unique ID for the Mailchimp list/audience.

inputs.name: is_syncing
inputs.about: Set to true to prevent this event from triggering automations. Useful when bulk-importing historical events.

inputs.name: properties
inputs.about: Optional key-value pairs of custom properties for the event. Example: {'product_name': 'T-Shirt', 'price': '29.99'}. Property names must be 2-30 characters.

inputs.name: occurred_at
inputs.about: The date and time the event occurred in ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2024-01-15T10:30:00Z'). Defaults to current time if not specified.

inputs.name: subscriber_hash
inputs.about: The MD5 hash of the lowercase version of the list member's email address. This endpoint also accepts a list member's email address or contact_id.

tools.name: Add export
tools.description: Create a new account export in your Mailchimp account. This action initiates an export of your Mailchimp account data as a downloadable ZIP file. The export runs in the background and may take from a few minutes to several hours depending on account size. Use the 'get_account_export_info' action with the returned export_id to check progress and retrieve the download URL. Important limitations: - Only one export can run at a time per account - Only one export can be created per 24-hour period - Completed exports are available for download for 90 days

inputs.name: include_stages
inputs.about: The types of data to include in the export. At least one stage is required. Available stages: 'audiences' (contact lists and segments), 'campaigns' (email campaign content), 'events' (contact activity events), 'gallery_files' (uploaded images and files), 'reports' (campaign performance reports), 'te

inputs.name: since_timestamp
inputs.about: Optional ISO 8601 timestamp to limit the export to data created after this time. Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+00:00 (e.g., '2024-01-15T00:00:00+00:00'). Note: This limit does NOT apply to audiences - all audience data is always included. Useful for incremental exports when you only need recent campai

tools.name: Upload File to File Manager
tools.description: Upload a new image or file to the Mailchimp File Manager. Use this action to upload files (images, documents, etc.) that can be used in campaigns, templates, or signup forms. The file must be base64-encoded and under 10MB. Supported image types: jpg, jpeg, gif, png, svg. Supported document types: pdf, txt, csv, and more. The uploaded file will be available at the returned full_size_url for use in your content.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The name of the file including extension (e.g., 'image.png', 'document.pdf'). This will be the display name in the File Manager.

inputs.name: file_data
inputs.about: The base64-encoded contents of the file to upload. The file must be a supported type (images: jpg, jpeg, gif, png, svg; documents: pdf, txt, csv, etc.) and under 10MB.

inputs.name: folder_id
inputs.about: The ID of the folder to upload the file to. If not provided, the file will be uploaded to the root folder.

tools.name: Add folder
tools.description: Create a new folder in the File Manager to organize uploaded files. Use this action to create organizational folders in the Mailchimp File Manager. Folders help organize images and other files that can be used in campaigns and templates.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The name of the folder to create in the File Manager. Must be unique within the account.

inputs.name: created_at
inputs.about: The date and time the folder was created in ISO 8601 format.

inputs.name: created_by
inputs.about: The username of the profile that created the folder.

inputs.name: file_count
inputs.about: The number of files in the folder.

tools.name: Add interest category
tools.description: Create a new interest category.

inputs.name: type
inputs.about: Determines how this category's interests appear on signup forms. Options: 'checkboxes' (multiple selection), 'dropdown' (single selection from dropdown), 'radio' (single selection from radio buttons), 'hidden' (not visible on forms).

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: The text description of this category. This field appears on signup forms and is often phrased as a question (e.g., 'What topics interest you?').

inputs.name: list_id
inputs.about: The unique ID for the list/audience to add the interest category to.

inputs.name: display_order
inputs.about: The order that the categories are displayed in the list. Lower numbers display first. Defaults to 0 if not specified.

tools.name: Add interest in category
tools.description: Create a new interest or 'group name' for a specific category.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The name of the interest (group name). This is shown publicly on subscription forms and used to group subscribers by their preferences.

inputs.name: list_id
inputs.about: The unique ID for the Mailchimp list/audience (e.g., 'abc123def4').

inputs.name: display_order
inputs.about: The display order for this interest within the category. Lower numbers display first. If not specified, the interest is added at the end.

inputs.name: interest_category_id
inputs.about: The unique ID for the interest category (group) where the interest will be added (e.g., 'xyz789ghi0').

tools.name: Add landing page
tools.description: Create a new Mailchimp landing page. Creates an unpublished landing page that can be customized and published later. Requires either a list_id or use_default_list=true. The landing page type can be 'signup' (for email list signups) or 'product' (for product promotions, requires store_id).

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The internal name of this landing page (for your reference, not visible to visitors).

inputs.name: type
inputs.about: The type of landing page template: 'signup' for email list signups, or 'product' for product promotions.

inputs.name: title
inputs.about: The title of this landing page displayed in the browser's title bar.

inputs.name: list_id
inputs.about: The audience/list ID to associate with this landing page. Either list_id or use_default_list=true must be provided.

inputs.name: store_id
inputs.about: The ID of the e-commerce store to associate with this landing page. Required for 'product' type pages.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: A brief description of this landing page for internal reference.

inputs.name: template_id
inputs.about: The specific template ID to use for this landing page. If not provided, a default template is used.

inputs.name: use_default_list
inputs.about: If true, creates the landing page using the account's default list instead of requiring a list_id. Either list_id or use_default_list=true must be provided.

inputs.name: tracking__track__with__mailchimp
inputs.about: Enable Mailchimp cookie tracking to monitor unique visitors and calculate conversion rates.

inputs.name: tracking__enable__restricted__data__processing
inputs.about: Enable Google's restricted data processing for CCPA compliance, limiting how Google uses certain identifiers and data in its services.

tools.name: Add list
tools.description: Create a new audience (list) in your Mailchimp account. This endpoint creates a new audience/list for managing email contacts. Each audience has unique settings for campaigns, permissions, and contact information. Note: Free Mailchimp accounts are limited to 1 audience. Paid plans allow multiple audiences. Required fields include: name, contact information (company, address1, city, country), permission_reminder, and campaign defaults (from_name, from_email, subject, language).

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The name of the audience/list. Must be unique within your Mailchimp account.

inputs.name: contact__zip
inputs.about: The postal or zip code for the list contact (optional).

inputs.name: double_optin
inputs.about: Whether to require double opt-in (subscriber must confirm via email). Recommended for GDPR compliance. Defaults to false.

inputs.name: contact__city
inputs.about: The city for the list contact. Required.

inputs.name: contact__phone
inputs.about: The phone number for the list contact. Optional.

inputs.name: contact__state
inputs.about: The state or province for the list contact (optional).

inputs.name: use_archive_bar
inputs.about: Whether campaigns for this list use the Archive Bar in archives by default. Defaults to false.

inputs.name: contact__company
inputs.about: The company name for the list. Required.

inputs.name: contact__country
inputs.about: A two-character ISO3166 country code (e.g., 'US', 'GB', 'CA'). Required.

inputs.name: contact__address1
inputs.about: The street address for the list contact. Required.

inputs.name: contact__address2
inputs.about: The secondary street address for the list contact (optional).

inputs.name: email_type_option
inputs.about: Whether subscribers can choose their email format (HTML vs plain-text). When true, subscribers choose their format. When false, all receive HTML with plain-text backup.

inputs.name: notify_on_subscribe
inputs.about: Email address to send subscribe notifications to. Provide a valid email address or omit to disable notifications.

inputs.name: permission_reminder
inputs.about: The permission reminder explaining why contacts are receiving emails from this list. Example: 'You are receiving this email because you opted in via our website.'

inputs.name: marketing_permissions
inputs.about: Whether to enable GDPR-friendly marketing permissions. Defaults to false.

inputs.name: notify_on_unsubscribe
inputs.about: Email address to send unsubscribe notifications to. Provide a valid email address or omit to disable notifications.

inputs.name: campaign__defaults__subject
inputs.about: The default subject line for campaigns sent to this list. Required.

inputs.name: campaign__defaults__language
inputs.about: The default language for this list's forms (e.g., 'en' for English). Required.

inputs.name: campaign__defaults__from__name
inputs.about: The default 'From' name for campaigns sent to this list. Required.

inputs.name: campaign__defaults__from__email
inputs.about: The default 'From' email address for campaigns sent to this list. Required.

tools.name: Add list member
tools.description: Create a new member in a Mailchimp audience without updating duplicates.

inputs.name: vip
inputs.about: Whether the subscriber has VIP status.

inputs.name: tags
inputs.about: Tag names to apply to the new member.

inputs.name: ip_opt
inputs.about: IP address used to confirm the subscriber's opt-in status.

inputs.name: status
inputs.about: Subscriber status: 'subscribed', 'unsubscribed', 'cleaned', 'pending', or 'transactional'.

inputs.name: list_id
inputs.about: The unique ID for the list.

inputs.name: language
inputs.about: Subscriber language preference as a two-letter ISO 639-1 code.

inputs.name: location
inputs.about: Subscriber latitude and longitude.

inputs.name: interests
inputs.about: Interest IDs mapped to whether the member opted in to each interest.

inputs.name: ip_signup
inputs.about: IP address the subscriber signed up from.

inputs.name: email_type
inputs.about: Type of email the member requested: 'html' or 'text'.

inputs.name: merge_fields
inputs.about: Merge-field values keyed by the audience's merge tags.

inputs.name: email_address
inputs.about: Email address for the subscriber.

inputs.name: timestamp_opt
inputs.about: When the subscriber confirmed opt-in, in ISO 8601 format.

inputs.name: timestamp_signup

Returns HTTP 204 No Content on success with an empty response body.

inputs.name: list_id
inputs.about: The unique ID for the list (audience). Can be obtained from the 'Get lists info' action.

inputs.name: subscriber_hash
inputs.about: The MD5 hash of the lowercase version of the list member's email address. This endpoint also accepts a list member's email address directly or the contact_id.

tools.name: Batch add or remove members
tools.description: Batch add or remove list members from a static segment in Mailchimp. This action allows you to efficiently manage membership in a static segment by adding and/or removing multiple email addresses in a single API call. Only works with static segments (not saved/dynamic segments based on conditions). Important notes: - At least one of members_to_add or members_to_remove must be provided - Email addresses must already exist as subscribers in the list - Non-existent emails are silently ignored (no error raised) - Maximum 500 emails can be processed per request for each operation - The segment must be a static segment (type='static'), not a saved segment

inputs.name: list_id
inputs.about: The unique ID for the Mailchimp list/audience. Obtain this using the 'Get lists info' or 'List segments' actions.

inputs.name: segment_id
inputs.about: The unique ID for the static segment. This must be a static segment, not a saved/dynamic segment. Obtain this using the 'List segments' action and filter by type='static'.

inputs.name: members_to_add
inputs.about: An array of email addresses to add to the static segment. Emails must already exist as subscribers in the list - non-existent emails are ignored. Maximum 500 emails per request. Example: ['user1@example.com', 'user2@example.com']

inputs.name: members_to_remove
inputs.about: An array of email addresses to remove from the static segment. Emails not in the segment are ignored. Maximum 500 emails per request. Example: ['user3@example.com', 'user4@example.com']

tools.name: Batch subscribe or unsubscribe
tools.description: Batch subscribe or unsubscribe list members.

inputs.name: list_id
inputs.about: The unique ID for the list.

inputs.name: members
inputs.about: An array of member objects. Each object must contain 'email_address' (string) and 'status' (one of: 'subscribed', 'unsubscribed', 'cleaned', 'pending', 'transactional'). Optional fields include: 'merge_fields' (dict with field tags like FNAME, LNAME), 'tags' (list of tag names), 'vip' (bool), 'langu

inputs.name: sync_tags
inputs.about: Whether this batch operation will replace all existing tags with tags in request.

inputs.name: update_existing
inputs.about: Whether this batch operation will change existing members' subscription status and data. Set to true to update existing members, false to only add new members. Defaults to false.

inputs.name: skip_duplicate_check
inputs.about: If skip_duplicate_check is true, we will ignore duplicates sent in the request when using the batch sub/unsub on the lists endpoint. The status of the first appearance in the request will be saved. This defaults to false.

inputs.name: skip_merge_validation
inputs.about: If skip_merge_validation is true, member data will be accepted without merge field values, even if the merge field is usually required. This defaults to false.

tools.name: Get Campaign Abuse Report Details
tools.description: Get detailed information about a specific abuse report for a campaign. An abuse complaint occurs when your recipient reports an email as spam in their mail program. This action retrieves the details of a specific abuse report including the email address that filed the complaint, the date of the report, and associated list information. Prerequisites: - You need a valid campaign_id (use 'list_campaigns' to find one) - You need a valid report_id (use 'retrieve_campaign_abuse_complaints' to list abuse reports)

inputs.name: fields
inputs.about: A comma-separated list of fields to return. Reference parameters of sub-objects with dot notation. Example: 'id,email_address,date'.

inputs.name: report_id
inputs.about: The unique ID of the abuse report to retrieve. This can be obtained from the 'retrieve_campaign_abuse_complaints' action which lists all abuse reports for a campaign.

inputs.name: campaign_id
inputs.about: The unique ID of the campaign. This can be obtained from the 'list_campaigns' action or from campaign reports.

inputs.name: exclude_fields
inputs.about: A comma-separated list of fields to exclude from the response. Reference parameters of sub-objects with dot notation.

tools.name: Campaign statistics feedback
tools.description: Get feedback based on a campaign's statistics. Advice feedback is based on campaign stats like opens, clicks, unsubscribes, bounces, and more.

inputs.name: fields
inputs.about: A list of fields to return. Reference parameters of sub-objects with dot notation (e.g., 'advice.type', 'advice.message').

inputs.name: campaign_id
inputs.about: The unique id for the campaign.

inputs.name: exclude_fields
inputs.about: A list of fields to exclude. Reference parameters of sub-objects with dot notation (e.g., '_links').

tools.name: Cancel campaign
tools.description: Cancel a Regular or Plain-Text Campaign after you send, before all of your recipients receive it. This feature requires Mailchimp Pro or Premium plan. IMPORTANT: This action can only be used on campaigns that are currently in the 'sending' status. It cannot be used on: - Draft campaigns (status: 'save') - Scheduled campaigns (status: 'schedule') - use Unschedule Campaign instead - Already sent campaigns (status: 'sent') - Paused campaigns (status: 'paused') When successful, the campaign status will change to 'canceling' and then 'canceled'. Any recipients who have already received the email will not be affected. Returns HTTP 204 No Content on success. Returns HTTP 402 Payment Required if account lacks Mailchimp Pro/Premium subscription. Returns HTTP 404 Not Found if campaign_id is invalid.

inputs.name: campaign_id
inputs.about: The unique id for the campaign to cancel. The campaign must be in 'sending' status (i.e., currently being delivered but not yet complete). You can obtain campaign IDs from the List Campaigns endpoint.

tools.name: Create a survey campaign
tools.description: Create a new email campaign that links to a specific survey in Mailchimp. This action generates a campaign based on an existing survey for a given audience/list. The survey must already exist in Mailchimp before creating a campaign for it. The created campaign will include a link to the survey, allowing recipients to participate. Prerequisites: - A valid Mailchimp audience/list (use 'Get lists info' to retrieve available lists) - An existing survey for that list (use 'Get information about all surveys for a list' to retrieve surveys) Returns the created campaign details including campaign ID, status, recipients, and settings.

inputs.name: list_id
inputs.about: The unique ID for the Mailchimp audience/list. This is a 10-character alphanumeric string (e.g., 'abc1234567'). You can obtain this from the 'Get lists info' action or from the Mailchimp dashboard.

inputs.name: survey_id
inputs.about: The unique ID for the survey to create a campaign for. This is a 10-character alphanumeric string (e.g., 'xyz9876543'). You can obtain this from the 'Get information about all surveys for a list' action.

tools.name: Customer journeys api trigger for a contact
tools.description: Trigger a Customer Journey step for a specific contact via the Mailchimp API. This endpoint allows you to programmatically activate an API trigger step in a Customer Journey for a given contact. Before using this action: 1. Create a Customer Journey in the Mailchimp app with an "API Trigger" as a starting point or step 2. Mailchimp will provide you with a URL containing the journey_id and step_id 3. Use those IDs along with the contact's email address to trigger the journey The contact must be a member of the audience associated with the Customer Journey. Returns HTTP 204 (No Content) on success with an empty response body.

inputs.name: step_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the step within the Customer Journey. This ID is provided by Mailchimp when you create an API trigger step in the Customer Journey builder.

inputs.name: journey_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the Customer Journey. This ID is provided by Mailchimp when you create an API trigger step in the Customer Journey builder.

inputs.name: email_address
inputs.about: The email address of the contact to trigger in the Customer Journey. The contact must be a member of the audience associated with the journey.

tools.name: Customize signup form
tools.description: Customize the appearance and content of a Mailchimp list's signup form. Use this action to modify the header text/image, body content sections, and CSS styles of the embedded signup form for a specific audience/list. The signup form is used to collect email subscriptions from website visitors.

inputs.name: styles
inputs.about: List of style customizations for form elements. Each item should have 'selector' (e.g., 'page_background', 'body_link_style') and 'options' (list of CSS property/value pairs like [{'property': 'background-color', 'value': '#ffffff'}]).

inputs.name: list_id
inputs.about: The unique ID for the Mailchimp list/audience whose signup form you want to customize.

inputs.name: contents
inputs.about: List of content sections for the signup form body. Each item should have 'section' (e.g., 'signup_message') and 'value' (the text content) keys.

inputs.name: header__text
inputs.about: The title/heading text displayed at the top of the signup form (e.g., 'Subscribe to Our Newsletter').

inputs.name: header__image__alt
inputs.about: Alternative text for the header image, used for accessibility and when the image cannot be displayed.

inputs.name: header__image__url
inputs.about: URL of the header image to display at the top of the signup form. Must be a publicly accessible image URL.

inputs.name: header__image__link
inputs.about: URL that users will be directed to when clicking the header image.

inputs.name: header__image__align
inputs.about: Horizontal alignment of the header image. Options: 'none', 'left', 'center', 'right'.

inputs.name: header__image__width
inputs.about: Width of the header image in pixels (e.g., '200').

inputs.name: header__image__height
inputs.about: Height of the header image in pixels (e.g., '100').

inputs.name: header__image__target
inputs.about: Target window for the header image link. '_blank' opens in new tab, 'null' opens in same window.

inputs.name: header__image__border__color
inputs.about: Color of the header image border in hex format (e.g., '#000000' for black).

inputs.name: header__image__border__style
inputs.about: CSS border style for the header image. Options: 'none', 'solid', 'dotted', 'dashed', 'double', 'groove', 'outset', 'inset', 'ridge'.

inputs.name: header__image__border__width
inputs.about: Width of the border around the header image in pixels (e.g., '2').

tools.name: Delete batch request
tools.description: Stops a batch request from running. Since only one batch request is run at a time, this can be used to cancel a long running request. The results of any completed operations will not be available after this call.

inputs.name: batch_id
inputs.about: The unique ID of the batch operation to stop/delete. This ID is returned when you create a batch request using the 'Start batch operation' endpoint.

tools.name: Delete batch webhook
tools.description: Permanently delete a batch webhook by its ID. Once deleted, the webhook URL will no longer receive POST notifications when batch operations complete. Use this action to remove webhooks that are no longer needed or to clean up invalid webhook endpoints. This action is idempotent - deleting a non-existent webhook returns a 404 error. Related actions: - list_batch_webhooks: Get all configured batch webhooks to find the ID - add_batch_webhook: Create a new batch webhook - update_batch_webhook: Modify an existing batch webhook's settings

inputs.name: batch_webhook_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the batch webhook to delete. This ID can be obtained from the 'list_batch_webhooks' action or from the response of 'add_batch_webhook'. Example: '1537c038e7'.

tools.name: Delete campaign
tools.description: Permanently delete a campaign from your Mailchimp account. This action removes the specified campaign and all associated data. Note: Only campaigns with 'save' or 'paused' status can be deleted. Campaigns that have been sent cannot be deleted.

inputs.name: campaign_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the campaign to delete. This can be obtained from the campaign list or campaign creation response.

tools.name: Delete campaign feedback message
tools.description: Remove a specific feedback message for a campaign.

inputs.name: campaign_id
inputs.about: The unique id for the campaign. Can be obtained from the list_campaigns action.

inputs.name: feedback_id
inputs.about: The unique id for the feedback message to delete. Can be obtained from the list_campaign_feedback or add_campaign_feedback actions.

tools.name: Delete campaign folder
tools.description: Delete a specific campaign folder from Mailchimp. When a campaign folder is deleted, all campaigns within that folder are automatically marked as 'unfiled' rather than being deleted. This operation is idempotent - deleting an already-deleted folder will return an error indicating the folder was not found. Returns HTTP 204 No Content on success.

inputs.name: folder_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the campaign folder to delete. This ID can be obtained from the list_campaign_folders or add_campaign_folder actions.

tools.name: Delete cart
tools.description: Delete a cart from an e-commerce store. This endpoint permanently removes a cart and all its line items from the specified store. Use this when a cart is no longer needed (e.g., after converting it to an order or when the customer has abandoned the checkout process). Note: Deleting a cart will cancel any pending abandoned cart automation emails associated with it. Carts do not automatically expire and will remain until deleted.

inputs.name: cart_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the cart to delete. This is the cart ID that was assigned when the cart was created. You can find cart IDs using the List Carts endpoint.

inputs.name: store_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the e-commerce store. This is the store ID you defined when creating the store using the Add Store endpoint.

tools.name: Delete cart line item
tools.description: Delete a specific line item from a cart in a Mailchimp e-commerce store. Cart line items represent products that a customer has added to their shopping cart. This action permanently removes a line item from the specified cart. The deletion cannot be undone - to restore the item, you would need to add it again using 'add_cart_line_item'. Use this action when: - A customer removes an item from their cart - You need to clear invalid or outdated line items - Syncing cart changes from your e-commerce platform to Mailchimp Note: If you need to delete the entire cart, use 'delete_cart' instead.

inputs.name: cart_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the cart containing the line item. You can get this from the 'list_carts' action or from the response when creating a cart.

inputs.name: line_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the line item to delete. You can get this from the 'list_cart_line_items' action or from the 'lines' array in cart details.

inputs.name: store_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the e-commerce store. You can get this from the 'list_stores' action or from the response when creating a store.

tools.name: Delete connected site
tools.description: Remove a connected site from your Mailchimp account. This action permanently deletes the specified connected site. Connected sites are external websites that have been linked to your Mailchimp account for tracking and integration purposes. Once deleted, the site tracking script will no longer collect data for this site. Note: This action is idempotent - deleting an already-deleted site will not cause an error but may return a 404 Not Found response.

inputs.name: connected_site_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the connected site to delete. This ID can be obtained from the List Connected Sites or Get Connected Site actions (returned as 'foreign_id').

tools.name: Delete customer
tools.description: Delete a customer from an e-commerce store. Permanently removes a customer record from the specified Mailchimp store. This action is destructive and cannot be undone. The customer's associated data including order history linkage will be removed, but existing orders will not be deleted. Returns HTTP 204 No Content on successful deletion.

inputs.name: store_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the e-commerce store. This is the ID assigned when the store was created in Mailchimp.

inputs.name: customer_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the customer within the store. This is the customer ID that was assigned when the customer was added to the store.

tools.name: Delete domain
tools.description: Delete a sending domain from the Mailchimp account's verified domains. This permanently removes a domain that was previously added for verification. The domain can be in any verification state (pending, verified, or authenticated). After deletion, the domain will no longer appear in the verified-domains list and cannot be used as a sender address until re-added and re-verified. Use 'list_sending_domains' to see available domains before deletion.

inputs.name: domain_name
inputs.about: The verified domain name to delete from the Mailchimp account (e.g., 'example.com').

tools.name: Delete file
tools.description: Permanently remove a file from the Mailchimp File Manager. This action deletes an image or document file from your Mailchimp account's File Manager. Once deleted, the file cannot be recovered. Files in the File Manager are typically used in campaigns, templates, or signup forms. IMPORTANT: This is a destructive action. Ensure you have the correct file_id before executing, as deletion is permanent. Files that are actively used in campaigns may still be accessible until those campaigns are deleted.

inputs.name: file_id
inputs.about: The unique numeric ID of the file to delete from the File Manager. You can get this ID from the 'List stored files' action or from the 'Add file' action response when uploading a new file.

tools.name: Delete folder
tools.description: Delete a specific folder in the File Manager. This permanently removes the folder and all files contained within it. Use with caution as this action cannot be undone.

inputs.name: folder_id
inputs.about: The unique ID of the File Manager folder to delete. This can be obtained from the list_folders action or from the response when creating a folder.

tools.name: Delete interest category
tools.description: Delete a specific interest category from a Mailchimp audience/list. Interest categories are used to group related interests together on signup forms (e.g., 'Newsletter Preferences', 'Product Interests'). Each category can contain multiple interests that subscribers can select. WARNING: This action permanently deletes the interest category and all interests within it. This cannot be undone. Any subscriber data associated with these interests will also be removed. Use this action when you need to: - Remove obsolete or unused interest categories - Clean up test data - Reorganize your list's interest structure Prerequisites: - Obtain the list_id using 'Get lists info' action - Obtain the interest_category_id using 'List interest categories' action

inputs.name: list_id
inputs.about: The unique ID for the Mailchimp audience/list containing the interest category. This is a 10-character alphanumeric string (e.g., '2cc9d141a8'). Retrieve available list IDs using the 'Get lists info' action.

inputs.name: interest_category_id
inputs.about: The unique ID for the interest category to delete. This is a 10-character alphanumeric string (e.g., 'a788d2f60b'). Retrieve available interest category IDs using the 'List interest categories' action. Note: Deleting an interest category will also delete all interests within it.

tools.name: Delete interest in category
tools.description: Delete a specific interest (group name) from an interest category within a Mailchimp list. This permanently removes the interest from the category. Returns HTTP 204 on success.

inputs.name: list_id
inputs.about: The unique ID for the list (audience) containing the interest category.

inputs.name: interest_id
inputs.about: The unique ID of the interest to delete within the category.

inputs.name: interest_category_id
inputs.about: The unique ID for the interest category containing the interest to delete.

tools.name: Delete landing page
tools.description: Permanently delete a Mailchimp landing page. This action permanently removes a landing page from your Mailchimp account. This operation cannot be undone. The landing page must exist and be in a deletable state (draft or unpublished). Published landing pages should be unpublished first before deletion. Returns a 204 No Content response on success, indicating the page was deleted. Returns a 404 error if the page_id does not exist.

inputs.name: page_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the landing page to delete. This is a 12-character hexadecimal string (e.g., '030001b4e1f0'). Use the List Landing Pages action to retrieve available page IDs.

tools.name: Delete list
tools.description: Permanently delete a list (audience) from your Mailchimp account. WARNING: This is a destructive and irreversible operation. Deleting a list will permanently remove all associated data including: - Subscriber email addresses and profile data - Subscriber activity history (opens, clicks, etc.) - Unsubscribe records - Complaint records - Bounce records - Segments and tags Export and backup your list data before deletion if needed. Returns HTTP 204 No Content on success.

inputs.name: list_id
inputs.about: The unique ID for the list (audience) to delete. This is a 10-character alphanumeric string (e.g., '2cc9d141a8'). Can be obtained from the GET /lists endpoint or list settings in Mailchimp.

tools.name: Delete list member
tools.description: Permanently delete a list member and all their personally identifiable information (PII). WARNING: This is an irreversible action. Once deleted, the member cannot be re-imported with the same email address. Use this for GDPR compliance or when permanently removing a contact. For soft removal (keeping the ability to re-add later), use archive_list_member instead. Returns HTTP 204 No Content on success with an empty response body.

inputs.name: list_id
inputs.about: The unique ID for the Mailchimp audience/list (e.g., 'abc123def4'). Can be obtained from the list_lists or get_lists_info actions.

inputs.name: subscriber_hash
inputs.about: The MD5 hash of the lowercase version of the list member's email address. For example, for 'User@Example.com', compute MD5 of 'user@example.com'. This hash is also returned as 'id' when adding or listing members.

tools.name: Delete merge field
tools.description: Delete a specific merge field (audience field) from a Mailchimp list/audience. WARNING: This action permanently deletes the merge field and all associated data collected from that field. This cannot be undone. Consider hiding the field from signup forms instead of deleting it. Back up your audience data before deleting. Note: Default merge fields (FNAME, LNAME, ADDRESS, PHONE) cannot be deleted.

inputs.name: list_id
inputs.about: The unique ID for the audience/list. Get this from the List Audiences endpoint (MAILCHIMP_GET_LISTS_INFO) or your Mailchimp dashboard.

inputs.name: merge_id
inputs.about: The numeric ID for the merge field to delete. Get this from the List Merge Fields endpoint (MAILCHIMP_LIST_MERGE_FIELDS). Note: Default fields like FNAME, LNAME, ADDRESS, and PHONE cannot be deleted.

tools.name: Delete note
tools.description: Delete a specific note for a list member in Mailchimp. Permanently removes a note associated with a subscriber. This operation cannot be undone. A successful deletion returns HTTP 204 No Content. To delete a note, you need: - list_id: The unique ID of the Mailchimp audience/list - subscriber_hash: The member's email address, MD5 hash of lowercase email, or contact_id - note_id: The unique ID of the note (can be obtained from list_recent_member_notes)

inputs.name: list_id
inputs.about: The unique ID for the Mailchimp list (audience).

inputs.name: note_id
inputs.about: The unique ID of the note to delete.

inputs.name: subscriber_hash
inputs.about: The MD5 hash of the lowercase version of the list member's email address. This endpoint also accepts the member's email address or contact_id directly.

tools.name: Delete order
tools.description: Permanently delete an order from a Mailchimp e-commerce store. This action removes the order and its associated line items. This operation cannot be undone.

inputs.name: order_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the order to delete within the specified store.

inputs.name: store_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the e-commerce store containing the order to delete.

tools.name: Delete order line item
tools.description: Delete a specific line item from an order in a Mailchimp e-commerce store. This action permanently removes the specified line item from the order. The operation is idempotent - deleting an already-deleted line item returns the same success response. Prerequisites: The store, order, and line item must exist. Use MAILCHIMP_LIST_STORES, MAILCHIMP_LIST_ORDERS, and MAILCHIMP_LIST_ORDER_LINE_ITEMS to find valid IDs. Note: This action cannot be undone. To add the line item back, use MAILCHIMP_ADD_ORDER_LINE_ITEM.

inputs.name: line_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the line item to delete from the order. Use MAILCHIMP_LIST_ORDER_LINE_ITEMS to find available line item IDs.

inputs.name: order_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for an order within the store. Use MAILCHIMP_LIST_ORDERS to find available order IDs for a store.

inputs.name: store_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the e-commerce store. Use MAILCHIMP_LIST_STORES to find available store IDs.

tools.name: Delete product
tools.description: Permanently delete a product from a Mailchimp e-commerce store. This action removes the product and all its variants. Returns HTTP 204 on success with no content. Use LIST_STORES to find store IDs and LIST_PRODUCT to find product IDs. This operation cannot be undone.

inputs.name: store_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the e-commerce store. Use LIST_STORES to find available store IDs.

inputs.name: product_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the product to delete. Use LIST_PRODUCT to find available product IDs for a store.

tools.name: Delete product image
tools.description: Delete a product image from a Mailchimp e-commerce store. This action permanently removes an image associated with a product. The operation is idempotent - deleting an already-deleted image will not cause an error. Before deleting, ensure you have the correct store_id, product_id, and image_id as this action cannot be undone.

inputs.name: image_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the product image to delete. This is the image ID you specified when adding the image to the product.

inputs.name: store_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the e-commerce store. This is the store ID you specified when adding the store to Mailchimp.

inputs.name: product_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the product within the store. This is the product ID you specified when creating the product.

tools.name: Delete product variant
tools.description: Delete a specific product variant from a Mailchimp e-commerce store. This action permanently removes a variant from a product. Use this to clean up discontinued variants or manage product options. Note that a product must always have at least one variant, so attempting to delete the last remaining variant of a product will fail. Prerequisites: - The store must exist (use list_stores to verify) - The product must exist in the store (use list_product to verify) - The variant must exist and not be the only variant for the product

inputs.name: store_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the Mailchimp e-commerce store containing the product variant to delete.

inputs.name: product_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the product that contains the variant to be deleted.

inputs.name: variant_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the specific product variant to delete. Note: A product must have at least one variant, so deleting the last variant may fail.

tools.name: Delete promo code
tools.description: Delete a promo code from an e-commerce store. This action permanently removes a specific promo code from a promo rule in a Mailchimp store. The promo code will no longer be available for customers to use. This action is idempotent - deleting an already-deleted promo code will not cause an error. Prerequisites: - The store must exist (use MAILCHIMP_LIST_STORES to verify) - The promo rule must exist in the store (use MAILCHIMP_LIST_PROMO_RULES to verify) - The promo code must exist within the promo rule (use MAILCHIMP_LIST_PROMO_CODES to verify) Note: This action is destructive and cannot be undone. The promo code will need to be recreated using MAILCHIMP_ADD_PROMO_CODE if you want to restore it.

inputs.name: store_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the e-commerce store. Use MAILCHIMP_LIST_STORES to retrieve available store IDs.

inputs.name: promo_code_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the promo code to delete. Use MAILCHIMP_LIST_PROMO_CODES to retrieve available promo code IDs for a promo rule.

inputs.name: promo_rule_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the promo rule that contains the promo code. Use MAILCHIMP_LIST_PROMO_RULES to retrieve available promo rule IDs for a store.

tools.name: Delete promo rule
tools.description: Permanently delete a promo rule from a Mailchimp e-commerce store. This action also removes all associated promo codes. Warning: This operation is irreversible. Returns HTTP 204 on success with no content body.

inputs.name: store_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the e-commerce store containing the promo rule to delete. Use MAILCHIMP_LIST_STORES to find available store IDs.

inputs.name: promo_rule_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the promo rule to delete. Use MAILCHIMP_LIST_PROMO_RULES to find promo rule IDs for a specific store.

tools.name: Delete segment
tools.description: Permanently delete a segment from a Mailchimp list (audience). This action removes the segment definition from the list. It does NOT delete the contacts/members within the segment - they remain in the list. Both static segments and saved segments can be deleted using this action. Note: This is a destructive operation that cannot be undone. Use with caution.

inputs.name: list_id
inputs.about: The unique ID for the Mailchimp list (audience) containing the segment. You can retrieve list IDs using the 'Get lists info' action.

inputs.name: segment_id
inputs.about: The unique ID of the segment to delete. You can retrieve segment IDs using the 'List segments' action. This can be either a saved segment (based on conditions) or a static segment (based on specific email addresses).

tools.name: Delete store
tools.description: Delete an e-commerce store from your Mailchimp account. WARNING: This is a destructive operation. Deleting a store will permanently remove all associated subresources, including Customers, Orders, Products, and Carts. This action cannot be undone. Returns HTTP 204 No Content on successful deletion.

inputs.name: store_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the e-commerce store to delete. This is the client-defined ID that was provided when the store was created (e.g., 'my-store-001').

tools.name: Delete template
tools.description: Permanently delete a user-created email template from your Mailchimp account. This action removes the specified template and cannot be undone. Only templates of type 'user' (custom templates you created) can be deleted. System templates and gallery templates cannot be deleted. Returns HTTP 204 No Content on success. Returns HTTP 404 if the template does not exist or is not a user template.
